raw_statement: By 31 December 2031, health spending by adults over 40 in high-income markets shifts measurably from episodic acute treatment toward continuous metabolic management and elective function-restoring procedures: (a) chronic GLP-1/metabolic therapy users exceed 40 million in the US/EU with median therapy duration over 24 months; (b) continuous glucose or equivalent biometric monitoring is used by a majority of diagnosed metabolic patients and a growing non-diagnosed cohort; and (c) robotic-assisted share of qualifying elective procedures (hernia, hysterectomy, prostate, joint) exceeds 50% in the US, with consumers actively researching device/platform choice pre-referral.
title: From Episodic Care to Continuous Metabolic Management and Consumer-Chosen Elective Procedures (2026–2031)

formalized.statement: By 31 December 2031, health consumption among adults 40+ in high-income markets measurably re-weights from episodic acute treatment toward (a) chronic pharmacological metabolic management, (b) continuous biometric telemetry, and (c) consumer-researched, device-differentiated elective function-restoring surgery. Operationally: >40m chronic GLP-1/incretin or successor metabolic-therapy users across the US+EU with median persistence >24 months; continuous glucose (or equivalent continuous metabolic biomarker) monitoring used by >50% of diagnosed metabolic patients plus a measurable non-diagnosed wellness cohort; robotic-assisted share of qualifying US elective procedures (inguinal/ventral hernia, benign hysterectomy, radical prostatectomy, total knee/hip) >50%, with documented pre-referral consumer platform research.
formalized.population: Adults aged 40+ in the US, EU-5, UK, Japan, Australia and Canada with insurance, national coverage or discretionary income sufficient for out-of-pocket chronic therapy; sub-populations: diagnosed obesity/T2D/pre-diabetes cohort, cardiometabolic-risk asymptomatic cohort, and elective-surgery candidates with degenerative or structural conditions.
formalized.behavior: Paying for and persisting with an ongoing therapeutic + measurement regimen (monthly injectable or oral metabolic agent, continuously worn sensor, app-mediated titration) in place of intermittent physician-initiated acute care; and, when surgery is needed, actively selecting hospital/surgeon by surgical platform brand before or during referral rather than accepting assignment.
formalized.observable_outcome: Three simultaneously satisfied thresholds: (a) US+EU chronic incretin/metabolic therapy prevalence >40m unique patients with >24-month median persistence (IQVIA/prescription-audit and payer PDC data); (b) CGM/continuous-biomarker penetration >50% of diagnosed metabolic patients plus >5m non-diagnosed users (device shipments, Dexcom/Abbott segment disclosure, OTC sensor units); (c) robotic share of the four named US elective procedure families >50% (Premier/Vizient/PINC AI hospital procedure coding, Intuitive procedure-volume disclosure), plus survey/search evidence that >25% of elective patients researched the surgical platform pre-procedure.
formalized.measurable_metric: Composite index: (1) chronic metabolic therapy patient count and median persistence months; (2) CGM units and continuous-biomarker users as % of diagnosed metabolic population; (3) robotic % of qualifying elective procedure volume; (4) share of medical-device/pharma spend classified as recurring-subscription-like versus episodic-encounter; (5) consumer search/intent volumes for procedure-platform terms as a proxy for pre-referral shopping.

mechanism.human_motivation: Fear of decline and desire for restored function and appearance; status signalling via visible body composition and visible technology; the deeper motive is control over an outcome (weight, glucose, mobility) that was previously experienced as fate. Aging cohorts with accumulated wealth buy healthspan before they buy anything else discretionary.
mechanism.friction_removed: Weekly/monthly self-administered therapy replaces clinic-dependent management; factory-calibrated sensors remove fingersticks and lab visits; telehealth and pharmacy-integrated prescribing remove the gatekeeping appointment; oral incretins remove needle aversion; minimally invasive/robotic technique removes the recovery-time and pain barrier that made elective surgery a last resort rather than a scheduled purchase.
mechanism.enabling_technology: Long-acting GLP-1/GIP and oral incretin chemistry with manufacturing scale-up; enzymatic subcutaneous sensors with 14–15 day wear and smartphone Bluetooth; closed-loop and titration algorithms; robotic surgical platforms with improving cost curves and competitive entrants (Hugo, Ottava, Versius) plus stapling/energy consumables; AI triage/coaching agents that make continuous data actionable rather than merely visible.
mechanism.economic_incentive: Manufacturers convert episodic revenue into multi-year annuity per patient; payers face the trade between $1–3k/yr net therapy cost and avoided cardiometabolic events, increasingly resolved by outcomes data and price erosion from competition and 2031 patent cliffs; hospitals amortize robotic capital across higher-throughput elective volume; patients pay cash where coverage is absent, revealing large out-of-pocket willingness to pay. Falling net price per patient is the main volume unlock.
mechanism.trust_requirement: Patients must trust (i) that chronic use of a drug in an otherwise healthy body is safe over decades, (ii) that sensor-derived numbers are accurate enough to act on, (iii) that data collected continuously will not be used against them in insurance, employment or litigation, and (iv) that the surgical platform they selected actually improves their outcome rather than the hospital's margin. Each is a separate failure surface.
mechanism.distribution_mechanism: Telehealth and compounding-successor prescribing channels, retail pharmacy and employer benefit design, national coverage decisions (CMS obesity coverage, NHS/European reimbursement), OTC sensor retail, direct-to-consumer advertising and social proof (before/after content, clinician influencers), and hospital marketing of robotic programs as a patient-acquisition tool.
mechanism.network_effects: Weak direct, strong indirect: social visibility of results drives peer adoption; aggregated sensor+outcome data improves titration algorithms and payer evidence; surgeon training volumes create a lock-in flywheel (trainees learn on the dominant platform, then demand it); ecosystem effects between drug, sensor, app and food/retail reformulation; consumer review and search infrastructure makes procedure-platform reputation legible and self-reinforcing.
mechanism.switching_costs: High for surgeons and hospitals (capital, consumables, credentialing, training hours); moderate for patients on therapy (weight regain on discontinuation creates biological lock-in — the single strongest retention mechanism in the thesis); low for sensors once form factors converge and reimbursement is portable; low for the drug molecule itself once generics/biosimilars and oral alternatives arrive after 2031.
mechanism.regulatory_constraints: Coverage decisions (CMS/Medicare Part D obesity, European HTA), label expansions (MASH, CV outcomes, OSA, CKD, addiction), FDA clearance of OTC/non-diagnostic sensors, compounding enforcement, DTC advertising rules, robotic-surgery reimbursement parity and any move to bundled/site-neutral payment that removes the hospital's incentive to buy platforms, plus privacy regimes (HIPAA gaps for wellness data, GDPR) governing continuous biometric telemetry.

analogues.name: Statins for primary prevention: mass chronic prophylaxis in asymptomatic adults
analogues.mechanism: A daily pill taken indefinitely by people who feel well, justified by a measured biomarker rather than symptoms; adoption required trusting a number and a long-horizon risk model, and was unlocked by guideline expansion plus price collapse at generic entry.
analogues.lesson: Biomarker-anchored chronic therapy in asymptomatic populations reaches enormous prevalence, but only after outcomes trials plus guideline codification plus generic pricing; the demand curve steepened sharply at price erosion, not at launch.

analogues.name: Antihypertensive therapy as lifelong management of an invisible condition
analogues.mechanism: Converting an asymptomatic measurement into a lifetime prescription and a home-measurement behavior; required primary-care infrastructure and patient acceptance of indefinite medication.
analogues.lesson: Persistence is the hard part, not initiation: real-world adherence settled far below trial adherence, which is the base case risk for the >24-month median persistence clause.

analogues.name: SSRIs (Prozac) and destigmatized chronic psychopharmacology
analogues.mechanism: A tolerable molecule plus cultural reframing converted an episodic, stigmatized, specialist-gated condition into routine primary-care chronic management with consumer pull.
analogues.lesson: Tolerability plus destigmatization expands the treated population far beyond the originally diagnosed one; the addressable market is defined by social acceptability, not epidemiology.

analogues.name: HIV antiretroviral therapy: acute fatal illness converted to chronic managed condition
analogues.mechanism: Therapy transformed episodic crisis care into continuous lifetime regimen with routine lab telemetry (viral load, CD4), fully re-plumbing where the spending occurs.
analogues.lesson: When efficacy is unambiguous, the acute-to-chronic conversion happens within a decade and permanently relocates the cost pool from hospitals to pharmacy and monitoring.

analogues.name: CGM and pump adoption in type 1 diabetes
analogues.mechanism: Continuous telemetry displacing episodic fingersticks; required sensor accuracy trust, reimbursement, and patient willingness to wear a visible device continuously.
analogues.lesson: Continuous monitoring reached majority penetration only after factory calibration, phone integration and CMS coverage; each of the three was necessary. Direct precedent for the CGM clause, and it took 15 years inside the most motivated cohort.

analogues.name: CGM expansion from type 1 into insulin-treated and then non-insulin type 2 diabetes
analogues.mechanism: Same telemetry extended to a much larger, less acutely motivated population as coverage widened and price fell; the transition from medical necessity to optional optimization.
analogues.lesson: Penetration into less-motivated cohorts tracks reimbursement almost exactly; where cash-pay, engagement decays within months. The non-diagnosed wellness cohort is the weakest leg of the thesis.

analogues.name: Consumer wearables: Fitbit to Apple Watch continuous biometric self-tracking
analogues.mechanism: Voluntary, cash-paid continuous body measurement adopted for status and self-optimization without any clinical mandate; complexity hidden behind a consumer interface.
analogues.lesson: Hardware ownership scaled but sustained behavior change did not; abandonment rates near half within a year. Device shipments overstate the 'continuous management' behavior the thesis requires.

analogues.name: DTC pharmaceutical advertising post-1997 FDA guidance: patient-initiated brand requests
analogues.mechanism: Consumers researching and naming a specific branded product before the clinical encounter, inverting the referral gate — structurally identical to pre-referral robotic platform shopping.
analogues.lesson: Once a medical product is consumer-legible and advertised, patient-initiated requests reach material share within ~5 years and physicians accommodate them the large majority of the time. The pre-referral shopping clause is the most likely leg to be satisfied early.

analogues.name: LASIK: elective, cash-pay, function-restoring procedure with consumer platform shopping
analogues.mechanism: Discretionary surgery bought like a consumer durable, advertised directly, with patients comparing laser technology brands and surgeon volume; entirely out-of-pocket.
analogues.lesson: Cash-pay elective procedures scale fast then plateau well below the eligible population and are brutally cyclical with consumer credit — a caution on the elective-volume assumption in a 5% rate regime.

analogues.name: Botox and injectable aesthetics: recurring maintenance treatment
analogues.mechanism: Converting one-off cosmetic intervention into a recurring quarterly subscription-like regimen with biological lock-in (results reverse on discontinuation) and strong social proof.
analogues.lesson: Reversal-on-discontinuation is the best retention mechanism in healthcare; it is exactly the mechanism (weight regain) underwriting the >24-month persistence clause.

analogues.name: Invisalign: consumer-brand-driven choice of a clinical platform
analogues.mechanism: Patients selecting the treatment technology and then finding a provider who offers it; manufacturer advertised past the clinician to the end user, creating provider pull.
analogues.lesson: Consumer brand pull over a clinical platform works but takes ~15 years and requires the manufacturer to fund provider training and consumer advertising simultaneously; incumbency in training is the moat.

analogues.name: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy displacing open surgery
analogues.mechanism: A minimally invasive technique replaced the open standard almost entirely, driven by patient demand for shorter recovery and surgeon competitive pressure, ahead of randomized evidence.
analogues.lesson: Technique substitution in surgery can exceed 80% share in under six years when recovery-time benefit is visible to patients; evidence follows adoption rather than leading it.

analogues.name: Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (da Vinci)
analogues.mechanism: Hospital capital purchase marketed directly to patients; patients traveled and self-selected for the robot, forcing non-adopting hospitals to buy in defensively.
analogues.lesson: Direct precedent and the strongest one: robotic share exceeded 85% of US prostatectomies within a decade on consumer-facing marketing despite contested outcome superiority. Hernia and gynecology have followed the same curve more slowly; joints are the open question because of implant-brand and bundled-payment dynamics.

analogues.name: Drug-eluting stents: rapid procedural technology substitution then evidence-driven correction
analogues.mechanism: A device upgrade captured the overwhelming majority of procedures within three years, then partially reversed on late-thrombosis safety signals and guideline revision.
analogues.lesson: Fast procedural adoption is reversible: a single safety or comparative-effectiveness publication can cut share sharply. Robotic and chronic-therapy adoption curves both carry this tail.

analogues.name: Hormone replacement therapy: mass chronic 'healthspan' therapy in asymptomatic women, then collapse
analogues.mechanism: Lifelong therapy sold on prevention and healthspan to a large well population; adoption reached mass scale and then fell by more than half within two years of the WHI trial readout.
analogues.lesson: The sharpest cautionary case: chronic therapy prescribed to healthy people for long-horizon benefit is hostage to one large outcomes trial. A negative long-term GLP-1 signal (muscle mass, bone, psychiatric, pancreatic) would break the persistence clause almost overnight.

analogues.name: Fen-phen and the first anti-obesity pharmacotherapy wave
analogues.mechanism: Identical motivation and identical consumer pull for weight-loss pharmacology, ended by valvulopathy withdrawal; followed by sibutramine and rimonabant withdrawals.
analogues.lesson: Demand for weight-loss pharmacology has never been the constraint — safety and durability have been, three times. The reference class for obesity drugs specifically is poor; incretins' CV-outcomes data is the only thing that distinguishes this attempt from the prior ones.

analogues.name: Orlistat/Alli OTC weight-loss switch
analogues.mechanism: Cash-pay, over-the-counter, consumer-initiated chronic weight management with mass advertising; failed on tolerability and modest efficacy.
analogues.lesson: Consumer intent plus distribution plus advertising is insufficient without efficacy that is visible within weeks; efficacy magnitude, not access, determines persistence.

analogues.name: Direct-to-consumer genomics (23andMe) as a self-directed health data purchase
analogues.mechanism: Consumers paying cash for personal biometric/biological data outside the clinical system, expected to drive continuous health behavior change; ended in one-shot curiosity purchases and a privacy/business-model collapse.
analogues.lesson: Health data without an actionable intervention loop does not create recurring behavior or recurring revenue, and continuous biological data accumulates privacy liability. The non-diagnosed CGM cohort must be bundled with a therapy or coaching loop to persist.

analogues.name: Perpetual-license to subscription conversion in software (Adobe, Autodesk, Microsoft)
analogues.mechanism: Non-medical structural analogue: one-off episodic transaction converted into a continuous metered relationship with telemetry, where the vendor gains an annuity and the customer trades ownership/control for continuous access and updates.
analogues.lesson: Episodic-to-continuous conversions re-rate the supplier's revenue quality dramatically before they show up in unit volumes; the investment return accrues to whoever owns the recurring relationship, not the product.

analogues.name: Total knee and hip arthroplasty as scheduled elective function restoration
analogues.mechanism: Degenerative condition treated by planned elective surgery bought for quality-of-life restoration, with growing patient awareness of implant and technique choice, later constrained by bundled payment and ASC migration.
analogues.lesson: Elective volume grows with demographics reliably, but payment reform (bundles, site-neutral, ASC shift) captures much of the value and actively penalizes expensive platform capital — the main structural threat to the >50% robotic joints clause.

reference_class.description: The reference class is 'episodic-to-continuous conversions of a health behavior in wealthy aging populations, plus consumer-directed selection of a clinical technology.' It has three sub-classes: (1) chronic pharmacotherapy adopted by largely asymptomatic people on the basis of a measured biomarker and long-horizon benefit (statins, antihypertensives, SSRIs, PPIs, HRT, ART); (2) continuous self-measurement technologies replacing episodic measurement (CGM in T1D then T2D, home BP, consumer wearables, DTC genomics); (3) consumer-pulled procedural/technology substitution in elective surgery (laparoscopy, LASIK, robotic prostatectomy, DES, Invisalign, arthroplasty). Base rates within the class: sub-class (1) and (3) converted successfully in the large majority of instances, with typical time-to-mainstream of 8–20 years and 3–8 years respectively; sub-class (2) succeeded only where reimbursement plus an actionable intervention loop existed, and failed where the data was decoupled from a therapy. The obesity-pharmacology sub-lineage specifically (fen-phen, sibutramine, rimonabant, orlistat) has a failure rate near 100% prior to incretins, making it the adversarial anchor.
reference_class.caveats: Selection bias: the successful analogues are the ones that produced durable franchises and are therefore over-remembered; the graveyard of chronic-therapy candidates is larger than the list above. The three thesis clauses are not independent in narrative but are quite independent in mechanism — the drug clause depends on price erosion and payer coverage, the sensor clause on reimbursement and bundling, the robotics clause on hospital capital cycles and payment reform — so a joint-satisfaction forecast should be materially below the minimum of the three marginals. Time compression is plausible (telehealth distribution, social proof velocity and manufacturing scale-up are faster than in any historical analogue) but the persistence clause has no historical precedent for a cash-pay chronic therapy at this price point, and real-world discontinuation in the first two commercial years has run far worse than trial adherence. HRT and DES show that a single outcomes readout can reverse a mass chronic or procedural behavior within 24 months, so the distribution is bimodal rather than smooth. Finally, the 2031 horizon sits at the leading edge of incretin patent expiry and site-neutral/bundled payment reform, which means the volume thesis and the pricing-power thesis may resolve in opposite directions.

evidence.claim: US GLP-1/incretin use for obesity and T2D has continued compounding; Lilly's tirzepatide franchise plus the first oral incretin (orforglipron) filings/launches have pushed combined US+EU chronic incretin users into the low-to-mid tens of millions trajectory, with oral formats removing needle aversion and cold-chain friction.
evidence.source: Company disclosures (LLY, Novo), IQVIA prescription audits, FDA action on oral GLP-1

evidence.claim: Real-world persistence remains the weak link: multiple claims-based studies (Prime Therapeutics, Blue Health Intelligence, Truveta) have repeatedly found ~50-70% of obesity-indication GLP-1 starters discontinue within 12 months, far short of the >24-month median persistence the thesis requires.

Biological lock-in is documented: SURMOUNT-4/STEP-1 extension data show ~two-thirds of lost weight regained within a year of discontinuation, which converts relapse into the strongest retention mechanism in consumer health and pushes persistence upward as net price falls.

Net price per patient is collapsing faster than volume is growing: direct-to-consumer cash channels (LillyDirect/NovoCare) at $349-499/month, TrumpRx-style most-favored-nation pricing deals and Medicare/Medicaid obesity pilots have cut effective cost per patient-year by well over half since 2023 — the primary volume unlock for a >40m user count.
evidence.source: Manufacturer DTC pricing, CMS obesity coverage pilot announcements

evidence.claim: Payer and employer retrenchment is running the other way: multiple state health plans, several large self-insured employers and some European HTA bodies have restricted or dropped obesity-indication coverage on budget-impact grounds, and a 5% risk-free rate plus consumer bifurcation constrains discretionary cash-pay at the margin.
evidence.source: Plan sponsor coverage decisions, NICE/G-BA restrictions, benefit consultant surveys

evidence.claim: OTC/non-prescription continuous glucose sensors (Dexcom Stelo, Abbott Lingo/Libre Rio) have been on sale in the US since 2024 and are being bundled into wellness, telehealth and GLP-1 programs, establishing a legitimate non-diagnosed cohort — the precondition for the >5m wellness-user threshold.

Clinical evidence that CGM changes outcomes in non-diabetic or non-insulin-treated users remains thin; several RCTs and editorials (JAMA Internal Medicine, Lancet D&E commentary) find little behavioural or glycaemic benefit, which caps reimbursement and makes the wellness cohort a fashion-dependent, churn-prone consumer category rather than infrastructure.

Robotic search intent surged 107% vs 28-day baseline with granular procedure-level queries (hysterectomy, hernia, prostate, knee replacement), evidencing pre-referral consumer platform shopping — the behavioural leg of the thesis and flagged as unpriced in our own attention dataset.

Procedure-level penetration is already past 50% in two of the four named families: robotic radical prostatectomy is ~85-90%+ of US cases and robotic benign hysterectomy plus inguinal/ventral hernia have crossed or approached half of qualifying volume, so the composite threshold hinges almost entirely on orthopaedics.
evidence.source: PINC AI/Premier hospital coding, ISRG procedure disclosures

evidence.claim: Total knee/hip arthroplasty robotic penetration is roughly 20-35% and migrating to ambulatory surgery centres where capital intensity, bundled payment economics and CMS site-neutral pressure argue against per-case robot cost; ortho robotics also lacks convincing outcome superiority data, which is exactly the pattern that stalled drug-eluting stents after the initial substitution wave.
evidence.source: SYK/ZB/Medtronic ortho disclosures, CMS ASC migration data

evidence.claim: Competitive entry is arriving on schedule — Medtronic Hugo US approval, J&J Ottava, CMR Versius, plus Chinese platforms — which lowers capital cost per system and broadens robotic access to community hospitals, the standard mechanism by which a premium technique becomes the default standard of care.
evidence.source: FDA clearances and company pipeline disclosures

evidence.claim: Label expansion into cardiovascular outcomes, MASH, sleep apnoea, CKD and knee osteoarthritis converts GLP-1s from a cosmetic/metabolic purchase into a reimbursable chronic prophylaxis — the exact statin pathway that produced 40m+ US chronic users over roughly 15 years.
evidence.source: SELECT, ESSENCE, SURMOUNT-OSA trial readouts and subsequent label changes

evidence.claim: Manufacturing and supply are no longer the binding constraint: multi-billion-dollar fill-finish and API capacity additions in Indiana, North Carolina and Ireland plus oral small-molecule chemistry have removed the 2023-24 shortage that suppressed initiation.
evidence.source: Manufacturer capex announcements, FDA shortage list resolution

evidence.claim: Continuous biometric telemetry has an unresolved trust failure surface: HIPAA does not cover wellness-device data, life/disability underwriting use is unregulated, and healthcare remains the most breached sector — a single high-profile misuse event could stall the non-diagnosed cohort the way 23andMe's collapse chilled consumer genomics.
evidence.source: FTC/OCR enforcement record, consumer genomics precedent

evidence.claim: The thesis is conjunctive across three independent thresholds; historically analogous mass-adoption waves (statins, CGM in T1D, laparoscopic cholecystectomy) each took 12-20 years to cross 50% penetration, and two of them (HRT, fen-phen) reversed outright on safety evidence — so simultaneous satisfaction by 2031 requires all three clocks to run at the fast end.
evidence.source: Reference-class base rates from the analogue set

prerequisites_met: Manufacturing scale-up and oral formulation removing supply and needle-aversion friction
Cardiovascular/MASH/OSA outcome labels converting cosmetic spend into reimbursable prophylaxis
OTC sensor clearance creating a legal non-diagnosed monitoring market
Robotic penetration already >50% in prostate and hysterectomy, establishing the standard-of-care template
Documented consumer pre-referral platform search behaviour
Falling net price per patient-year via DTC cash channels and MFN-style pricing
prerequisites_missing: Median therapy persistence >24 months — current real-world discontinuation is the single largest gap
Durable payer/CMS coverage for obesity indication at scale in both US and EU
Outcome evidence justifying CGM in non-diagnosed users (no evidence, no reimbursement, high churn)
Orthopaedic robotic economics that survive ASC migration and bundled payments
A settled privacy/underwriting regime for continuous biometric data
Surgeon training throughput on non-Intuitive platforms
stage.historical_pathway_position: Roughly where statins sat circa 1997-2001 (post-outcomes-trial, pre-generic, coverage fights live) for the drug leg; where CGM sat in T1D circa 2016 for the diagnosed-monitoring leg; and where laparoscopic cholecystectomy sat circa 1993 for soft-tissue robotics but only circa 1988 for orthopaedics. The composite is mid-early-majority with the ortho and persistence legs lagging by roughly five years.

bull.description: Oral incretins at sub-$200/month net plus CMS and European obesity coverage push US+EU chronic users through 40m by 2029-30; relapse-driven lock-in plus GLP-1-bundled CGM coaching lifts median persistence past 24 months; Hugo/Ottava price competition collapses robot capital cost and ortho robotics crosses 50% as ASC-compatible compact systems ship. All three thresholds clear by 2031 and health becomes an explicit subscription category — a per-patient annuity of $2-4k/year across ~50m people, with device consumables and adherence infrastructure capturing a rising share as molecule price erodes.

base.description: Two of three clear. Chronic metabolic therapy reaches roughly 25-38m US+EU users with median persistence improving to 14-20 months (real but short of 24); CGM exceeds 50% of diagnosed metabolic patients on the back of Libre/Stelo price declines and GLP-1 bundling, with a 3-8m wellness cohort that churns; robotic share exceeds 50% in the soft-tissue triad but orthopaedics stalls in the 30-40% band. Direction of travel is unambiguous and the spending mix shifts materially toward recurring, but the strict conjunctive test fails on the persistence and ortho legs.

bear.description: Payer retrenchment under a 5% cost-of-capital regime, a safety signal in long-duration asymptomatic use (the HRT/fen-phen pattern), or an outcomes-evidence disappointment in the non-diabetic cohort caps prevalence near 20-25m with persistence stuck around 12 months; CGM in the non-diagnosed collapses to a fitness fad after a data-misuse or underwriting scandal; bundled payment and ASC migration strand hospital robotic capital, and the 2031-33 semaglutide/tirzepatide patent cliffs turn the annuity into a low-margin generic commodity before the behavioural shift is locked in. Health spending re-weights modestly, but the value pool deflates faster than it migrates.

supporting: Median persistence (PDC/days-on-therapy) in claims data rising above 18 months for obesity-indication starters
CMS national obesity coverage decision and EU-5 HTA reimbursement approvals
Oral incretin net price per month falling below $200 with launch volumes outrunning injectable cannibalisation
OTC sensor unit shipments exceeding prescription CGM growth and a non-diagnosed user base disclosed above 3m
Medtronic Hugo and J&J Ottava installed base and procedure counts entering quarterly disclosure
Robotic share of total knee arthroplasty in PINC AI/Premier coding crossing 40%
Hospital marketing spend and consumer search volume for named surgical platforms continuing to compound
Employer benefit surveys showing obesity-drug coverage inclusion rising rather than falling
contradictory: New discontinuation studies keeping 12-month persistence below 50%
Large employers or state plans publicly dropping obesity coverage; PBM formulary exclusions
A randomized readout showing no benefit of CGM in non-insulin or non-diagnosed populations
CMS site-neutral/bundled payment rules that penalize per-case robotic cost in ortho
Any long-duration safety signal (muscle mass, bone density, psychiatric, thyroid, pancreatic) in asymptomatic chronic users
Intuitive procedure growth decelerating below mid-teens, indicating saturation rather than expansion
Accelerating ASC migration of joint replacement without compact robotic platforms
A major biometric-data misuse or underwriting scandal
indicators.next_confirmation_signal: The next two quarters of real-world persistence data alongside the first full year of oral incretin scripts: if 12-month discontinuation drops below 45% while oral volumes are additive rather than substitutive, the 24-month persistence threshold becomes reachable and the whole composite re-rates. Concurrently watch the first CMS ruling on obesity coverage scope.
biggest_variables: Persistence/adherence — the single binary that determines whether this is an annuity or a churn business
Net price trajectory versus payer budget impact under a high-rate, fiscally constrained regime
Long-duration safety in asymptomatic users (the HRT reversal risk)
Orthopaedic robotic economics under bundled payment and ASC migration
Whether continuous biometric data becomes trusted infrastructure or a liability
The 2031-33 patent cliff timing relative to behavioural lock-in

value_pools.emerging_need: A multi-decade prophylactic taken by otherwise healthy adults, priced and distributed like a consumer subscription
value_pools.opportunity: Owner of the dominant incretin franchise with oral optionality captures a per-patient annuity, but pricing power erodes each year toward the 2031-33 cliff

value_pools.emerging_need: Actionable, low-friction telemetry for both diagnosed patients and a wellness cohort with no reimbursement
value_pools.opportunity: Sensor unit volume explodes while ASP per sensor collapses; the winner is whoever attaches to the drug regimen and the coaching algorithm, not the hardware margin

value_pools.emerging_need: Function-restoring elective surgery chosen by the patient, with the platform as a consumer-legible brand
value_pools.opportunity: Installed base converts to a per-procedure consumable annuity; surgeon training throughput and credentialing are the real moat, and competitive entry compresses system price not consumable price

value_pools.emerging_need: Persistence is the binding constraint; whoever raises median months-on-therapy creates the entire annuity
value_pools.opportunity: AI titration and behavioural-nudge layers embedded in pharmacy, payer and device workflows — the highest-leverage unpriced layer in the thesis

value_pools.layer: Biometric data security and privacy governance
value_pools.emerging_need: Continuously streamed physiological data outside HIPAA, exposed to underwriting, employment and litigation misuse
value_pools.opportunity: Health-data-specific security and consent infrastructure becomes non-discretionary; a single misuse scandal is the thesis's kill-switch and the sector's demand catalyst

value_pools.layer: On-device inference for continuous health telemetry
value_pools.emerging_need: Always-on sensing and coaching that cannot afford cloud latency, cost per token or privacy exposure
value_pools.opportunity: Edge silicon and phone/watch platforms become the default compute substrate for metabolic telemetry, capturing the margin cloud AI expected

value_pools.layer: Payer utilization management and risk pricing
value_pools.emerging_need: Underwriting a population whose pharmacy trend is structurally higher but whose acute event rate falls with a multi-year lag
value_pools.opportunity: Whoever prices the trade between $1-3k/yr therapy and avoided events first wins share; whoever misprices it blows up a quarter

value_pools.layer: Pharma manufacturing, fill-finish and life-science tooling
value_pools.emerging_need: Sustained capacity for peptide API, oral small-molecule and autoinjector volumes at 40m-patient scale
value_pools.opportunity: Contracted, capital-intensive supply with multi-year backlogs — the physical chokepoint of the metabolic annuity

value_pools.layer: Food, beverage and retail calorie supply
value_pools.emerging_need: 20-40m adults with structurally suppressed appetite and shifted basket composition toward protein and portion control
value_pools.opportunity: Reformulation and protein/GLP-1-companion SKUs; scale grocers and clubs adapt, branded snack and sugared-beverage volume is the donor

value_pools.layer: Cold chain and specialty pharmacy logistics
value_pools.emerging_need: Monthly recurring delivery of temperature-sensitive or high-value therapy direct to tens of millions of homes
value_pools.opportunity: Recurring, contracted, density-advantaged parcel volume; oral formats partially disintermediate cold chain but raise total shipment count

second_order_thesis: The consensus trade is to own the molecule. The second-order insight is that the molecule is the most competed, most price-eroded and soonest-expiring part of the stack — the thesis's own mechanism (biological relapse on discontinuation) creates an annuity whose economics accrue not to whoever discovered the peptide but to whoever owns persistence. Value migrates from the chemistry to (i) the adherence layer that turns a 12-month median into a 30-month median, (ii) the per-procedure consumable and surgeon-training flywheel in robotics, where switching costs are institutional rather than personal and therefore durable through a rate shock, and (iii) the trust infrastructure around continuous biometric telemetry, which is the thesis's single largest failure surface and therefore its largest mandatory-spend category. Sensors follow the classic hardware path: volumes up an order of magnitude, ASP down, margin captured by whatever the sensor attaches to. Meanwhile the thesis is conjunctive across three clocks running at different speeds — soft-tissue robotics is already past the line, orthopaedics is a decade behind, and persistence is the unresolved binary — so the honest position is to own the legs that are already inflecting (robotic consumables, edge-inference substrate, health-data security, contracted manufacturing) and to treat the >40m/>24-month drug threshold as the low-probability leg rather than the anchor. Finally, this is one of the few structural demand stories that is genuinely counter-cyclical to a 5% risk-free rate: aging, wealthy cohorts defund travel, housing turnover and branded snacking before they defund restored function, which makes the calorie-supply and episodic-care complex the funding source for the entire shift.
losers: Branded snack, confection and sugared-beverage volume as appetite suppression scales — MDLZ, PEP, KO, and to a lesser extent MCD and SBUX on visit frequency
Managed care and pharmacy-benefit underwriters that mispriced the pharmacy trend versus the lagged acute-event offset — UNH most exposed
Hospitals and health systems without robotic programs or brand-legible platforms, which lose elective share to consumer-shopped competitors and ASCs
Legacy fingerstick blood-glucose meters, test strips and episodic lab-draw diagnostics
Bariatric surgery volumes and CPAP/sleep-apnoea device franchises facing pharmacological substitution
Sensor hardware pure-plays with no attached coaching, drug or payer relationship as CGM ASPs commoditize — DXCM's standalone margin is the clearest expression
Incretin originators post-2031 patent cliff if persistence has not locked in a switching-cost moat before generics arrive — LLY and peers on terminal value, not near-term earnings
Orthopaedic implant makers whose robot capital is stranded by ASC migration and bundled payment — SYK carries the highest exposure to this specific failure mode
Episodic acute-care-levered providers, urgent care roll-ups and dialysis/CKD-progression-dependent businesses

probability.note: Posterior log-odds = prior log-odds (reference-class base rate) + sum of quality x independence weighted log likelihood ratios. Research-informed estimate until enough theses resolve for Brier calibration.

source_bullets.text: Health shifts from episodic treatment to continuous measurement: CGM and device-based monitoring become default infrastructure for metabolic health and healthspan.

Health is shifting from episodic treatment to continuous measurement and metabolic management: Novo rebranding and 'rethinking' strategy amid the GLP-1 war, plus continuous glucose monitoring, reflect consumers buying ongoing healthspan rather than acute care.

Health: demand is shifting from drugs to procedures and devices \u2014 robotic-surgery search interest up 107% vs 28-day with granular intent (hysterectomy, hernia, prostate, knee), Medtronic raising guidance on heart-device demand. People want restored function and healthspan, not just managed disease, and they are researching the machine that will operate on them.

Health is being re-framed as a procedure-and-device consumption decision: the 107% surge in robotic-surgery queries spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee replacement is an aging population actively shopping for less-invasive interventions, and the dataset flags it as unpriced.

Health behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacological metabolic management (Lilly gaining GLP-1 share, Novo's injectables deal) and away from device-and-discipline models, which raises the bar for CGM and continuous-monitoring franchises to prove incremental value.
